subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: After the remaining cooldown propagation defects are fixed, should OpenClaw accept persistent provider-scoped `inline-api-key:<provider>` cooldown state and fail-closed inline API-key behavior during auth/billing backoff?
rationale: The implementation is a real fix for a P1 retry spiral, but it changes upgrade behavior for existing inline-key users and adds durable auth-state/API surface that code review cannot approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept after repair
options.body: Fix the remaining propagation and hook-isolation defects, then merge the provider-scoped cooldown behavior as the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep the bug fix but avoid or hide the public helper and require a smaller internal-only cooldown surface before merge.

options.title: Pause for auth design
options.body: Do not merge this branch until maintainers choose a different recovery or cooldown design for inline provider credentials.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the remaining propagation and hook-isolation defects, then merge the provider-scoped cooldown behavior as the intended compatibility contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest recent history across the auth resolution files and is the best available routing owner for the compatibility contract decision.
